title: Exam Mix 02 — Applied Practice
description: Mixed revision: relational rules, ER modelling and keys, normalisation, and SQL.

items.question: A university tracks attendance separately for each student in each course. A student can enrol in several courses, and a course can have many students. The database stores one ENROLMENT row for each student–course pair. The university stores one attendance percentage per student per course. Which table should store AttendancePercentage?
items.explanation: AttendancePercentage belongs in ENROLMENT because it describes one student in one course. A student can have different attendance percentages in different courses, and students in the same course can have different percentages. Neither STUDENT nor COURSE identifies the student–course pair.

references.label: Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer, p. 15
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: A bookstore user has already reviewed a book. The REVIEWS primary key is (User_ID, Book_ID). What prevents that user from adding a second review for the same book?

options.text: The same key pair would be repeated
The user ID can never appear in another review
The book ID can never appear in another review
All reviews must have the same date

items.explanation: The pair must be unique. Either ID may appear again with a different partner.

items.question: STUDENT_ENROLL has SID 21 with sportNO 1 and SID 34 with sportNO NULL. SPORT has (1, swimming). With students on the left, what sport name accompanies SID 34 after LEFT JOIN on sportNO?
items.explanation: The left row is retained, but there is no matching sport row to supply a name.

items.question: Biology 1 appears in several records in a combined student–class table. The school renames it, but one occurrence is missed. Which symptom shows the update anomaly?

options.text: A new class cannot be inserted
Deleting a student removes the class
The same class now has inconsistent names
The table is sorted by student

items.explanation: Only some copies of the same fact were changed, leaving two names for Biology 1.

items.question: The Mini Café buys the same ingredient from different suppliers at different prices. Which record should hold the supplier-specific price?
items.explanation: The price belongs to the arrangement between a specific supplier and a specific ingredient.

items.question: A numeric height column contains the entry “between 168 and 171”. In the lecture’s 1NF height example, what is wrong with that entry?

options.text: It is a text range rather than a single numeric height

items.explanation: The numeric column is for individual numeric heights, not a textual range.

items.question: Given STUDENT_ENROLL on the left and SPORT on the right, a sport has no matching student. In a RIGHT JOIN on sportNO, what appears for the student name on that sport’s result row?

options.text: An empty row is not returned

items.explanation: The right-side sport row is preserved; the unmatched student columns are NULL.

items.question: The Week 4 process converts a table from 1NF to 2NF. A non-key attribute depends on just one column of a two-column primary key. What should happen to that attribute?

options.text: Leave it because all cells are atomic
Remove the key that really determines it
Duplicate it in every matching row
Move it to a table keyed by the column that determines it

items.explanation: 2NF removes partial dependencies by separating the attribute with the part of the key that determines it.

items.question: In the Mini Library, every title must have one or more physical copies. A BOOK_TITLE row has no associated BOOK_COPY rows. Does this satisfy the rule?

options.text: No; each title must have at least one physical copy
Yes; only the maximum number of copies matters
Yes; copies are required only after the first loan
No; every title must have exactly two copies

items.explanation: BR4 sets the minimum at one copy and allows multiple copies per title.
